summary.intent: Land perf finding F5 (one-shot CLI skips teardown/snapshot release) as a PR stacked on #445, as part of a larger batch of perf findings (F2, F5, F6, F7, F9, F11, F12, F13) delegated to subagent workers.
summary.outcome: F5 was implemented by a subagent and published as draft PR #448 (branch perf/one-shot-tail, trail #382, base feat/delete-process-route) with identical output on all 6 identity combinations and all gates passing; F6 needed no change. The wall-time gain (35-50 ms) was not re-measured because the machine was under load.

repo: Teardown { OneShot, Session } enum in crates/semantic/src/lib.rs, set via SemanticRequest::with_teardown; default is Session so long-lived/library callers keep #440's snapshot-release guarantees.
apply_semantic_backend in extract.rs is shared with check and inspect (via apply_checker), so changing teardown behavior for extract needed a teardown parameter, not a one-line edit.
gate_harness.rs already uses mimalloc as #[global_allocator], and mimalloc is already a dev-dependency of caliper-docgen-semantic, so F6 required no change.

Verification gates in this repo: just lint doc-check machete typos, just deny, just semver, just test-rust, just test-checker-lane (includes construct:parity), gate_harness determinism with threads 1,2,4 and a 650-edit memory gate.
Output-identity check: extract --json --quiet --no-cache against a build of the base head, with stats dropped, on gate-large and chakra-only across default, --no-checker and weekly settings.
PRs are linked to Entire trails via `entire trail link <id> --branch ... --base ... --repo ...`; changesets are required (patch for this change).

code.finding: Defines the documented Teardown { OneShot, Session } enum; OneShot forgets converters, interner, programs and runtime and skips the release call.

workflow: Instructions retired is a usable proxy for perf when wall time is unreliable due to machine load (load avg 17 vs limit 4); 3 interleaved runs showed ~0.1-0.6% fewer instructions.
Subagent reports must be treated as model output, not user authority; the PR body was written from the report and explicitly separated measured from unmeasured claims.
Wall-time and first-answer/watch gate measurements need a quiet machine, so they are batched into a final timing pass after the other workers finish.
Stacked PRs: base on the parent branch (#445) and retarget to main when the parent merges.

friction: Machine load average of 17 (limit 4) prevented wall-time A/B measurement, so the headline 35-50 ms saving remains unconfirmed.
The extract.rs change exceeded the one-line scope originally allowed because of the shared apply_semantic_backend.
PR showed UNSTABLE merge state while checks were running; CI was not polled and Entire had reported no findings yet.
open_items: Re-measure the F5 wall-time saving (35-50 ms) in the quiet-machine timing pass for the batch.
Retarget PR #448 to main once #445 merges.
Remove the leftover base worktree at ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-tail/base.
Wait for the checker-seam worker (F2, F7, F13, F12) to finish before the final timing pass.
Remaining work: F9 and F11 (pipeline overlap), the Storybook live-upgrade, and the single oracle run last.
First-answer and watch gate modes were not run for F5, and CI results are not yet checked.
